what: DERIVATION, independent attempt 3 of 5: The halo of a producing lump: its strength against the lump's record count. SETTING (blocks 39, 40, 41; open PRs titled 'ail39: records that move', 'ail40', 'ail41: what a source is'): records move and carry their content; a site is empty or holds one record (content = one of the six axes); two neighbouring records weigh W = c * omega (omega = p, q, r for equal, opposite, orthogonal contents), a bond with an empty end weighs 1, a record weighs z; the neutral scale is c_0 = 6/(p+q+4r), at which every row of W sums to 6 and records do not bind on any window without a cycle (all binding is the loop factor 1 + 3 l_1^n + 2 l_2^n, l_1 = (p-q)/(p+q+4r), l_2 = (p+q-2r)/(p+q+4r)). Motion: a record hops to an empty neighbour, choosing between its two positions in proportion to the pair weights it would have there (an isolated record hops symmetrically). Formation: an empty site x forms a record at rate z Z_x, Z_x = sum over contents a of the product of W(a, s_y) over the recorded neighbours y, content drawn in proportion to the summand; records are never removed. BLOCK 41 PROVED: (1) the only local additive invariant density is the occupancy: mass = number of records; (2) two sets of records separated by empty sites weigh the product of their weights, at any scale: no action across empty sites; (3) the field of a held record through a medium is the pair correlation, of short range (ladder exact; cubic lattice about one step or less away from the clumping onset); (4) the content field around a record is a number times its content vector, zero for a record of unread content: the mass has no charge in the long-range tilt channel; (5) under symmetric hops with one record per site d<n_x>/dt = kappa * (lattice Laplacian of <n>)_x + j_x exactly, j the mean formation rate, so a steady excess of production carries the stationary halo G * (j - mean j)/kappa with G the lattice Green function (one-over-distance on Z^3); at the neutral scale the formation rate next to ONE record is exactly the void's (Z_x = 6), next to records of independent uniform contents it is the void's on average, and next to k agreeing records it is larger by 6^(k-1) (p^k+q^k+4r^k)/(p+q+4r)^k (13/12, 5/4 at (3,1,2); 46/21, 2348/343 at (12,1,2); k = 2, 3). NOT YET KNOWN: what a lump's halo looks like, how strong it is, and what a second lump does inside it. TASK: a lump is a finite set of records held in place with agreeing contents (all +z) at the neutral scale; empty sites form records at rate z Z_x and free records hop symmetrically at rate kappa. (a) The production excess of the lump is Q = z * sum over empty sites x next to the lump of (Z_x - 6). Show that an empty site touching exactly one record contributes 0, so that a cube (every outside neighbour touches one record) has Q = 0 exactly, and compute Q in closed form for: a cube with one record removed from a face (a pit), a cube with one record added on a face (an adatom), a staircase surface, a lattice ball of radius R (leading order in R: surface or volume?), and a porous lump in which each site of a cube is occupied independently with probability f (leading order: proportional to the record count?). (b) State and prove the halo: in the dilute limit the stationary excess mean occupancy is u(x) = (1/kappa) sum_y G(x - y) q_y with q_y the excess at y; give the far field Q/(4 pi kappa |x|) and the first correction (the dipole of q). (c) Say what changes when the lump's contents do NOT agree (independent uniform contents: mean excess 0; give the variance of Q), and what the sign of Q can be (Z_x < 6 next to disagreeing records: a sink of production). (d) Decide whether Q proportional to the record count is possible for any family of lumps, and state the condition. An exact check.py must verify (a) on explicit lumps by enumeration.  DELIVERABLE, in your unit worktree on ai/probes: probes/work/derive/source-halo-of-a-producing-lump/<your worker name>/ATTEMPT.md and check.py. ATTEMPT.md: (1) the exact statement you attempt; (2) numbered steps, each marked PROVED (argument given in full), CHECKED (a finite fact check.py verifies exactly) or ASSUMED; (3) if the route fails, the FIRST step that fails and why: a precise no-go for a route is a result; (4) what would finish it. check.py: exact arithmetic (fractions, integers, sympy) for every finite claim; it prints `SUMMARY: PROVED ...`, `SUMMARY: COUNTEREXAMPLE ...`, `SUMMARY: PARTIAL <what is new and exact>` or `SUMMARY: ROUTE FAILS AT <step>`, and a line `HIT: <the claim>` ONLY when you claim a proof, a counterexample, or a new exact partial result others can build on; a HIT is handed to a worker of another model family to referee line by line, so write for a hostile reader. Rules: definitions come from the notes on the PR branches named above (git fetch origin <branch>; git show origin/<branch>:<note>; find them with gh pr view <n> --json files,headRefName); any outside theorem you use must be re-proved at the scope you use it or listed under ASSUMED; no status words (proved theorems are promoted by the supervisor after the referee). Have your own plan BEFORE reading the prior attempts printed at claim time; then either build on a refereed partial result or take a different route. Run: python3 probes/run_probe.py <task> --worker <name> --model <model> --review "..." --extra "python3 probes/work/derive/source-halo-of-a-producing-lump/<name>/check.py"
